label: def:span
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:span}
    For a finite set $\mathcal{X}$ and $U\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{X}}$, the span seminorm is $\|U\|_{\mathcal{X},\mathrm{sp}}:=\max_{x\in\mathcal{X}}U(x)-\min_{x\in\mathcal{X}}U(x)$. This is used on $\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}}$ and $\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{A}}$, and for $\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}}$ we write $\|Q\|_\mathrm{sp}:=\|Q\|_{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A},\mathrm{sp}}$. We also define the \emph{action-span seminorm} $\|Q\|_\mathrm{asp}:=\max_{s\in\mathcal{S}}\|Q(s,\cdot)\|_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{sp}}$. Both vanish on constants, $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{asp}$ vanishes on every $Q$ that depends only on the state, and $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$.

label: def:union_graph
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:union_graph}
    The \emph{union graph} $G$ is the directed graph on $\mathcal{S}$ with an edge $s\to s'$ whenever $p(s'|s,a)>0$ for some $a\in\mathcal{A}$. For $X\subseteq\mathcal{S}$ and $k\geq0$, $XG^k$ is the set of states reached from $X$ by a walk of length exactly $k$. $G$ is \emph{primitive} if it is strongly connected and aperiodic, and its \emph{exponent} $\mathrm{ex}(G)$ is then the smallest $k\geq1$ such that $\{s\}G^k=\mathcal{S}$ for every $s$.

label: prop:mixing_characterization
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:mixing_characterization}
    For every full-support $\mu$, \@gobble{assumption:m-step-mixing} holds for some $m$ if and only if $P_\mu$ is irreducible and aperiodic, if and only if $G$ is primitive, if and only if the MDP is communicating and $G$ is aperiodic. In particular, \@gobble{assumption:m-step-mixing} holds with some full-support policy if and only if it holds with every full-support policy: whether it holds only depends on the support of $p$, and $\mu$ only affects its constants $\beta_m$ and $\nu$.
head: environment

title: Proof
body_md: The second equivalence holds because $G$ is the support graph of $P_\mu$, and the third because $G$ is strongly connected if and only if the MDP is communicating. If $\underline{V}^m_\mu>0$, then $P^m_\mu>0$ and $P^{m+1}_\mu>0$ entrywise, so $P_\mu$ is irreducible, with closed walks of lengths $m$ and $m+1$ through every state, hence aperiodic. Conversely, if $G$ is primitive, then $\{s_1\}G^{\mathrm{ex}(G)}=\mathcal{S}$ for every $s_1$, so that, for $m:=\mathrm{ex}(G)+1$ and any $s_1$ with $p(s_1|s,a)>0$, $K^m_\mu(\cdot|s,a)\geq p(s_1|s,a)P^{m-1}_\mu(\cdot|s_1)>0$, i.e.\ $\underline{V}^m_\mu>0$.

label: prop:minimal_horizon
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: The minimal horizon

title: Proof
body_md: By the first-step decomposition and the full support of $\mu$, $K^m_\mu(\cdot|s,a)>0$ if and only if $X_{s,a}G^{m-1}=\mathcal{S}$, with $X_{s,a}:=\mathrm{supp}\,p(\cdot|s,a)$. As $G$ is strongly connected, every state has a predecessor, so $XG^k=\mathcal{S}$ implies $XG^{k+1}=\mathcal{S}$, and $\{k\mid XG^k=\mathcal{S}\}=\{k\geq e(X)\}$. Hence $\underline{V}^m_\mu>0$ if and only if $m-1\geq e(X_{s,a})$ for every $(s,a)$, which gives the formula. Since $e(X)\leq\mathrm{ex}(G)$ for every nonempty $X$, $m^*\leq\mathrm{ex}(G)+1$; since $P^{m^*}_\mu(s'|s)=\sum_a\mu(a|s)K^{m^*}_\mu(s'|s,a)>0$ for every $(s,s')$, $m^*\geq\mathrm{ex}(G)$; and $\mathrm{ex}(G)\leq(|\mathcal{S}|-1)^2+1$ by \citet{wielandt1950}.

label: rem:mixing_comparison
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:mixing_comparison}
    Under \@gobble{assumption:m-step-mixing}, the MDP is communicating (\@gobble{cor:mixing_implies_span}) and every full-support policy induces an irreducible aperiodic chain (\@gobble{prop:mixing_characterization}). The assumption is thus equivalent to the standard one on the behavior policy of asynchronous $Q$-learning, a full-support policy inducing an irreducible aperiodic chain \citep[Assumption~3.1]{chen2025nonasymptotic}. \citet{chen2025nonasymptotic} additionally assumes that the Bellman operator is a span contraction (his Assumption~2.1), whereas we obtain the contraction from regularization toward $\mu$, and the constants of $\mu$ enter the rates. It is incomparable with the unichain condition: two states swapped by a single action form a unichain MDP whose $G$ is periodic, and adding a self-loop action makes $G$ primitive but the MDP not unichain. Unlike the unichain condition, whose verification is NP-hard \citep{tsitsiklis2007nphard}, it is checked in polynomial time on $G$, and it is preserved by adding actions or transitions. Periodicity can be removed by laziness, i.e.\ replacing $p(\cdot|s,a)$ by $\frac12(\delta_s+p(\cdot|s,a))$, which preserves the gain of every stationary policy. Finally, if $P_\mu$ is unichain and aperiodic but has transient states, then for $m$ large enough $\beta_m$ is still positive but $\nu$ vanishes exactly on these states, which a trajectory following full-support policies visits finitely often: full support of $\nu$ is what makes single-trajectory learning possible on every pair.

label: convention:product_order
title: Convention
body_md:
\label{convention:product_order}
    Throughout, $\mathcal{X}$, $\mathcal{Y}$ and $\mathcal{Z}$ denote finite sets, typically $\mathcal{S}$ or $\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}$, and $P$ is a row-stochastic matrix from $\mathcal{X}$ to $\mathcal{Y}$. It maps functions $f\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{Y}}$ to $Pf\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{X}}$ and distributions $\phi\in\Delta(\mathcal{X})$ to $\phi P\in\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$:
    \[
        (Pf)(x)=\sum_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}P(y|x)f(y), \qquad (\phi P)(y)=\sum_{x\in\mathcal{X}}\phi(x)P(y|x).
    \]
    The product of $P_1$ from $\mathcal{X}$ to $\mathcal{Y}$ and $P_2$ from $\mathcal{Y}$ to $\mathcal{Z}$ is $(P_1P_2)(z|x)=\sum_{y\in\mathcal{Y}}P_1(y|x)P_2(z|y)$, so that $(P_1P_2)f=P_1(P_2f)$ and $\phi(P_1P_2)=(\phi P_1)P_2$. In a product $P_1P_2\cdots P_n$, the Markov chain therefore takes its first step with $P_1$ and its last with $P_n$, whereas a function is transformed first by $P_n$ and last by $P_1$.

head: environment
name: Self-bounding lower tail

title: Proof
body_md:
This is the lower tail of the multiplicative Azuma inequality \citep[App.~A]{kuszmaul2021multiplicative}, stated on the event $\{\bar{S}\geq a\}$ in the manner of \citet{freedman1975tail} rather than under an almost-sure lower bound on $\bar{S}$; we recall the argument.
    Let $\theta>0$ and $p_i:=\mathbb{E}[Z_i/b\mid\mathcal{G}_{i-1}]$. Convexity of $y\mapsto e^{-\theta y}$ on $[0,1]$ and $1-x\leq e^{-x}$ give $\mathbb{E}[e^{-\theta Z_i/b}\mid\mathcal{G}_{i-1}]\leq1-p_i(1-e^{-\theta})\leq e^{-p_i(1-e^{-\theta})}$, so that $M_k:=\exp\big(-\frac{\theta}{b}\sum_{i\leq k}Z_i+(1-e^{-\theta})\sum_{i\leq k}p_i\big)$ is a non-negative supermartingale with $M_0=1$.
    On the event $\{S<c,\ \bar{S}\geq a\}$ we have $M_B\geq\exp\big(-\frac{\theta c}{b}+(1-e^{-\theta})\frac{a}{b}\big)$, so Markov's inequality bounds its probability by $\exp\big(\frac{1}{b}(\theta c-(1-e^{-\theta})a)\big)$, which is minimized at $\theta=\log(a/c)$; this is~\eqref{eq:exact-chernoff}.

label: lem:dobrushin_doeblin
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:dobrushin_doeblin}
    Let $\mathcal{X}$ and $\mathcal{Y}$ be finite and let $P$ be a row-stochastic matrix from $\mathcal{X}$ to $\mathcal{Y}$. If there exist $\beta\in(0,1]$ and $\nu\in\Delta(\mathcal{Y})$ with $P(y|x)\geq\beta\nu(y)$ for all $(x,y)\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$, then $\alpha(P)\leq 1-\beta$.
head: environment
name: Doeblin and Dobrushin coefficients

title: Proof
body_md:
This is classical \citep[\S4.3]{seneta2006nonnegative}; we recall the argument.
    Since $|a-b|=a+b-2\min\{a,b\}$ and both rows sum to one, $\|P(\cdot|x)-P(\cdot|x')\|_{\mathrm{TV}}=1-\sum_{y}\min\{P(y|x),P(y|x')\}$ for all $x,x'\in\mathcal{X}$.
    Each minimum is at least $\beta\nu(y)$ by the minorization, so the sum is at least $\beta$ and every row distance is at most $1-\beta$.

label: lem:terminal_action
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:terminal_action}
    Let $n\geq1$, let $\pi_1,\dots,\pi_n$ be policies and $K:=K_{\pi_1}\cdots K_{\pi_n}$, the chain taking its first step with $K_{\pi_1}$ (\@gobble{convention:product_order}). If $\pi_k\geq\gamma_k\mu$ for $k\in\llbracket1,n-1\rrbracket$ and $K^n_\mu(\cdot|s,a)\geq\beta\nu$ for every $(s,a)$, then $\alpha(K)\leq1-\beta\prod_{k=1}^{n-1}\gamma_k$.
head: environment
name: The terminal action does not affect the contraction

title: Proof
body_md: The rows of $K$ factor as $K(s',a'|x)=A(s'|x)\,\pi_n(a'|s')$, where $A(\cdot|x)$ is the law of the $n$-th state. The terminal factor being common to all rows, $1-\alpha(K)=\min_{x,y}\sum_{s'}\min\{A(s'|x),A(s'|y)\}=1-\alpha(A)$. Only the $n-1$ intermediate actions enter $A$, so the transport inequality $P_{\pi_k}\geq\gamma_kP_\mu$ gives $A(\cdot|x)\geq\big(\prod_{k=1}^{n-1}\gamma_k\big)K^n_\mu(\cdot|x)\geq\beta\big(\prod_{k=1}^{n-1}\gamma_k\big)\nu$, and \@gobble{lem:dobrushin_doeblin} concludes.

label: lem:spop
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Operator span seminorm

title: Proof
body_md:
Assume $A\mathbf{1}\notin\mathbb{R}\mathbf{1}$, i.e.\ $\|A\mathbf{1}\|_\mathrm{sp}>0$. For every $c>0$ the vector $c\mathbf{1}$ satisfies $\|c\mathbf{1}\|_\mathrm{sp}=0\leq1$, while $\|A(c\mathbf{1})\|_\mathrm{sp}=c\|A\mathbf{1}\|_\mathrm{sp}\to+\infty$ as $c\to+\infty$. Hence $\|A\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{op}}=+\infty$.

    Conversely, the span seminorm vanishes exactly on the constant vectors, so it induces a norm, still denoted $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$, on the quotient spaces $E_{p}:=\mathbb{R}^{p}/\mathbb{R}\mathbf{1}$ and $E_{q}:=\mathbb{R}^{q}/\mathbb{R}\mathbf{1}$.
    Under (ii), the factorization theorem gives that $A$ induces a well-defined linear map $\tilde{A}:E_{p}\to E_{q}$, $\tilde{A}[f]=[Af]$.
    By construction $\|Af\|_\mathrm{sp}=\|\tilde{A}[f]\|_\mathrm{sp}$ and $\|f\|_\mathrm{sp}=\|[f]\|_\mathrm{sp}$, so $\|A\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{op}}$ is the operator norm of $\tilde{A}$ between the normed spaces $(E_{p},\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp})$ and $(E_{q},\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp})$, which is finite since $E_{p}$ is finite-dimensional.

    Finally, the first inequality in~\eqref{eq:sub-multiplicativity} is the operator-norm inequality $\|\tilde{A}[f]\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq\|\tilde{A}\|\,\|[f]\|_\mathrm{sp}$. For the second, $AB$ also satisfies (ii) and induces the map $\tilde{A}\tilde{B}$, and operator norms are submultiplicative.

label: lem:row-stochastic-span
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:row-stochastic-span}
    Let $P\in\mathbb{R}^{q\times p}$ be row-stochastic. Then its operator span seminorm equals its Dobrushin coefficient, $\|P\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{op}}=\alpha(P)$, and consequently $\|Pf\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq\alpha(P)\|f\|_\mathrm{sp}$ for every $f\in\mathbb{R}^p$.
head: environment
name: Span seminorm of a row-stochastic matrix

title: Proof
body_md:
Since $P$ is row-stochastic, $P\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}$, so $P$ satisfies condition~(ii) of \@gobble{lem:spop}: $\|P\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{op}}$ is finite, and the last claim follows from~\eqref{eq:sub-multiplicativity} once the equality is proved.
    For $f\in\mathbb{R}^p$ we have $\|Pf\|_\mathrm{sp}=\max_{i,j}\left\{(Pf)_i-(Pf)_j\right\}=\max_{i,j}\sum_k\left(P_{ik}-P_{jk}\right)f_k$.

    Fix $i,j$, let $c_k:=P_{ik}-P_{jk}$, and let $I^+$ (resp.\ $I^-$) be the set of indices $k$ with $c_k\geq0$ (resp.\ $c_k<0$). Since $P$ is row-stochastic, $\sum_kc_k=0$, hence $C:=\sum_{k\in I^+}c_k=-\sum_{k\in I^-}c_k=\frac{1}{2}\sum_k|c_k|$, and with $\overline{f}:=\max_kf_k$ and $\underline{f}:=\min_kf_k$, $\sum_kc_kf_k=\sum_{k\in I^+}c_kf_k+\sum_{k\in I^-}c_kf_k\ \leq\ C\overline{f}-C\underline{f}=C\|f\|_\mathrm{sp}$.
    Maximizing over $(i,j)$ and using \@gobble{def:tv_norm,def:dobrushin} gives $\|Pf\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq\frac12\max_{i,j}\sum_k|P_{ik}-P_{jk}|\,\|f\|_\mathrm{sp}=\alpha(P)\|f\|_\mathrm{sp}$, i.e.\ $\|P\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{op}}\leq\alpha(P)$.

    If $\alpha(P)=0$ there is nothing to prove, so assume $\alpha(P)>0$ and let $(i^*,j^*)$ attain the maximum defining $\alpha(P)$. The coefficients $c_k:=P_{i^*k}-P_{j^*k}$ are not all zero and sum to zero, so they take both signs, and the vector $f^*$ defined by $f^*_k:=1$ if $c_k\geq0$ and $f^*_k:=0$ otherwise is non-constant, with $\|f^*\|_\mathrm{sp}=1$. Then $\|Pf^*\|_\mathrm{sp}\ \geq\ (Pf^*)_{i^*}-(Pf^*)_{j^*}=\sum_{k\in I^+}c_k=\frac{1}{2}\sum_k|P_{i^*k}-P_{j^*k}|=\alpha(P)$, hence $\|P\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{op}}\geq\alpha(P)$.

label: prop:mvi-span
title: Proposition
head: environment
name: Mean value inequality in span seminorm

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\pi:\mathbb{R}^q\to E_q:=\mathbb{R}^q/\mathbb{R}\mathbf{1}$ be the quotient map, $E_q$ being normed by $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$ as in the proof of \@gobble{lem:spop}, and let $h:=Q-Q'$.
    By (H1) the curve $g(t):=\pi(\Phi(Q(t)))$ is differentiable on $[0,1]$ with $g'(t)=\pi(D\Phi(Q(t))h)$, and by (H2) and~\eqref{eq:sub-multiplicativity}, $\|g'(t)\|_\mathrm{sp}=\|D\Phi(Q(t))h\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq\|D\Phi(Q(t))\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathrm{op}}\|h\|_\mathrm{sp}$.
    The mean value inequality for differentiable curves in a normed space \citep[\S8.5]{dieudonne1960foundations} gives $\|g(1)-g(0)\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq\sup_{t\in(0,1)}\|g'(t)\|_\mathrm{sp}$, which is~\eqref{eq:mvi-span} since $\|g(1)-g(0)\|_\mathrm{sp}=\|\Phi(Q)-\Phi(Q')\|_\mathrm{sp}$.

label: lem:omega_star_props
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:omega_star_props}
    For each $s\in\mathcal{S}$, let $\Omega_s:\Delta(\mathcal{A})\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}$ be proper, closed and strongly convex, and let $\sigma>0$ be a common modulus of strong convexity of the $\Omega_s$ with respect to $\|\cdot\|_1$, which exists by equivalence of norms on $\mathbb{R}^\mathcal{A}$ and finiteness of $\mathcal{S}$; let $\tau\geq0$ and $Q,Q'\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}}$.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item \emph{Greedy policy}: if $\tau>0$, $\Omega^*(\cdot)(s)$ is differentiable, $\nabla\Omega^*(Q)(s)=\pi_{\Omega,Q}(\cdot|s)$ is the unique maximizer in its definition, and $\|\pi_{\Omega,Q}(\cdot|s)-\pi_{\Omega,Q'}(\cdot|s)\|_1\leq\frac{1}{2\tau\sigma}\|Q_s-Q'_s\|_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{sp}}$.
        \item \emph{Boundedness}: if $L_{\Omega_s}\leq\Omega_s\leq U_{\Omega_s}$ on $\mathrm{dom}(\Omega_s)$, then $\Omega^*(Q)(s)\leq\max_aQ_s(a)-\tau L_{\Omega_s}$; if moreover $\delta_a\in\mathrm{dom}(\Omega_s)$ for every $a\in\mathcal{A}$, then $\Omega^*(Q)(s)\geq\max_aQ_s(a)-\tau U_{\Omega_s}$.
        \item \emph{Translation equivariance}: $\Omega^*(Q+c\mathbf{1})=\Omega^*(Q)+c\mathbf{1}$ for every $c\in\mathbb{R}$.
        \item \emph{Monotonicity}: if $Q_s\leq Q'_s$, then $\Omega^*(Q)(s)\leq\Omega^*(Q')(s)$.
        \item \emph{Non-expansiveness in $\|\cdot\|_\infty$}: $\|\Omega^*(Q)-\Omega^*(Q')\|_{\mathcal{S},\infty}\leq\|Q-Q'\|_{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A},\infty}$.
        \item \emph{Non-expansiveness in $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$}: $\|\Omega^*(Q)-\Omega^*(Q')\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}\leq\|Q-Q'\|_{\mathrm{sp}}$.
        \item \emph{Sub-affinity in $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$}: $\|\Omega^*(Q)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}\leq\|Q\|_{\mathrm{sp}}+\|\Omega^*(0)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}$.
    \end{enumerate}

name: Properties of $\Omega^*$

title: Proof
body_md:
\phantomsection\hypertarget{proof:omega_star_props}{}
    \emph{(i)}. $\Omega^*(\cdot)(s)$ is the convex conjugate of the closed, $\tau\sigma$-strongly convex function $\tau\Omega_s$, so it is differentiable, its gradient is the unique maximizer, and this gradient is $\frac{1}{\tau\sigma}$-Lipschitz from $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ to $\|\cdot\|_1$ \citep{kakade2012regularization}; see \citet[\S E.4]{hiriart2001fundamentals} for the Euclidean case and \citet[Prop.~1]{geist2019theory} for $\Omega_s$ finite on $\Delta(\mathcal{A})$. Adding a constant to $Q'_s$ shifts the objective by that constant and leaves the maximizer unchanged, so the bound holds with $\|Q_s-Q'_s-c\mathbf{1}\|_\infty$ for every $c\in\mathbb{R}$, and $\min_{c\in\mathbb{R}}\|Q_s-Q'_s-c\mathbf{1}\|_\infty=\frac12\|Q_s-Q'_s\|_{\mathcal{A},\mathrm{sp}}$.

    \emph{(ii)}. This refines \citet[Prop.~1]{geist2019theory}, where $\Omega_s$ is finite on the whole simplex. For every $\pi_s\in\mathrm{dom}(\Omega_s)$, $\langle\pi_s,Q_s\rangle\leq\max_aQ_s(a)$ and $\tau\Omega_s(\pi_s)\geq\tau L_{\Omega_s}$; taking the supremum gives the upper bound. For the lower bound, let $a^\star\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_aQ_s(a)$: since $\delta_{a^\star}\in\mathrm{dom}(\Omega_s)$, $\Omega^*(Q)(s)\geq\max_aQ_s(a)-\tau\Omega_s(\delta_{a^\star})\geq\max_aQ_s(a)-\tau U_{\Omega_s}$.

    \emph{(iii)--(iv)}. For every $\pi_s\in\Delta(\mathcal{A})$, $\langle\pi_s,Q_s+c\mathbf{1}\rangle=\langle\pi_s,Q_s\rangle+c$, and $\langle\pi_s,Q_s\rangle\leq\langle\pi_s,Q'_s\rangle$ when $Q_s\leq Q'_s$ since $\pi_s\geq0$; take the supremum over $\pi_s$.

    \emph{(v)}. This is the argument of \citet{crandall1980some}. With $C:=\|Q-Q'\|_{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A},\infty}$, we have $Q'-C\mathbf{1}\leq Q\leq Q'+C\mathbf{1}$, and (iii)--(iv) give $\Omega^*(Q')-C\mathbf{1}\leq\Omega^*(Q)\leq\Omega^*(Q')+C\mathbf{1}$.

    \emph{(vi)}. The same argument with $c:=\min_{s,a}(Q-Q')(s,a)$ and $C:=\max_{s,a}(Q-Q')(s,a)$ gives $\Omega^*(Q')+c\mathbf{1}\leq\Omega^*(Q)\leq\Omega^*(Q')+C\mathbf{1}$, whence $\|\Omega^*(Q)-\Omega^*(Q')\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}\leq C-c=\|Q-Q'\|_{\mathrm{sp}}$. Maps that are monotone and translation equivariant are called topical, and are non-expansive for both norms \citep{lemmens2012nonlinear}.

    \emph{(vii)}. By the triangle inequality and (vi) with $Q'=0$, $\|\Omega^*(Q)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}\leq\|\Omega^*(Q)-\Omega^*(0)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}+\|\Omega^*(0)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}\leq\|Q\|_{\mathrm{sp}}+\|\Omega^*(0)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}$.

label: rem:strict_convexity
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:strict_convexity}
    We keep strong convexity in \@gobble{assumption:convex-analytic-regularity}, as is standard since \citet{geist2019theory}, but our results only use part of it.
    Uniqueness and continuity of the greedy map, and continuous differentiability of $\Omega^*$, i.e.\ \@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(i) without its Lipschitz constant, hold under strict convexity alone: $\tau\Omega_s$ is closed with bounded domain, so $\Omega^*(\cdot)(s)$ is finite and convex, its subdifferential, the set of maximizers, is a singleton \citep[\S E.4]{hiriart2001fundamentals}, and a differentiable convex function is continuously differentiable \citep[Cor.~25.5.1]{rockafellar1970convex}.
    This is all that \@gobble{lem:mixing-properties-of-regularization}, the mean value inequality (\@gobble{prop:mvi-span,cor:avg}), the existence of the fixed point (\@gobble{thm:regularized_fixed_point}) and the finite-time bounds of \@gobble{sec:results} require, so they hold verbatim for strictly convex regularizers; the modulus only enters the Lipschitz constant of \@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(i).
    For instance, the $\alpha$-divergences with $\alpha>2$ are strictly but not strongly convex (\@gobble{thm:alpha}.(ii)); they fail~\eqref{eq:P1}, but their $\epsilon$-floored versions satisfy it (\@gobble{lem:floor_wrapped_props}.(iii) only needs a strictly convex base), and our results apply to them.

title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:span_to_sup}
    Adding a constant to $Q_s$ shifts the objective defining $\Omega^*(Q)(s)$ by that constant, so $\pi_{\Omega,Q+c\mathbf{1}}=\pi_{\Omega,Q}$: as for the unregularized relative $Q$-function \citep{puterman1994markov}, the greedy policy depends on $Q$ only modulo constants, which is why the analysis is carried out in $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$. The centering projection $\Pi$ turns span convergence into convergence in $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ to the representative $\Pi[Q^*_\Omega]$: since $\Pi[Q]-\Pi[Q']$ has zero mean, $\|\Pi[Q]-\Pi[Q']\|_\infty\leq\|\Pi[Q]-\Pi[Q']\|_\mathrm{sp}=\|Q-Q'\|_\mathrm{sp}$. A centering step plays the same role for asynchronous average-reward $Q$-learning in \citet{chen2026pointwise}, where it upgrades span-seminorm convergence to pointwise convergence at the same rate.

\label{cor:T_omega_props}

title: Proof
body_md:
\phantomsection\hypertarget{proof:T_omega_props}{}

Since $P\geq0$ and $P\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}$, monotonicity and translation equivariance follow from \@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(iii)--(iv), and non-expansiveness from (v)--(vi), $P$ being non-expansive in $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ and, as $\alpha(P)\leq 1$ (\@gobble{lem:row-stochastic-span}), in $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$. Finally, by \@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(i), $\partial \mathcal{T}_\Omega(Q)(s,a)/\partial Q(s',a')=p(s'|s,a)\,\pi_{\Omega,Q}(a'|s')=K_{\pi_{\Omega,Q}}(s',a'|s,a)$, which is continuous in $Q$.

label: def:mixing_objects
title: Definition
body_md:
\label{def:mixing_objects}
    Let $\Omega$ satisfy \@gobble{assumption:convex-analytic-regularity}, let $\mu$ be the mixing policy of \@gobble{assumption:m-step-mixing}, let $Q,Q'\in\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}}$, $Q(t):=tQ+(1-t)Q'$ for $t\in[0,1]$, and $R\geq0$.
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item \emph{Average-path policy}: $\bar{\pi}_{\Omega,[Q,Q']}:=\int_0^1\pi_{\Omega,Q(t)}\,\mathrm{d}t$ is the mean greedy policy along the segment $[Q',Q]$.
        \item \emph{Average-path radius}: $R[Q,Q']:=\max_{t\in[0,1]}\|Q(t)\|_\mathrm{asp}$ is the largest action span along the segment; by convexity of $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{asp}$, it equals $\max\{\|Q\|_\mathrm{asp},\|Q'\|_\mathrm{asp}\}$.
        \item \emph{Domination profile}: $\gamma_\Omega(R):=\inf\big\{\pi_{\Omega,Q}(a|s)/\mu(a|s) \mid (s,a)\in\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A},\ \|Q\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq R\big\}$ is the largest factor such that $\pi_{\Omega,Q}\geq\gamma_\Omega(R)\,\mu$ for every $Q$ of action span at most $R$. It lies in $[0,1]$, is non-increasing in $R$, and governs contraction and exploration (\@gobble{lem:mixing-properties-of-regularization}).
        \item \emph{Regularization modulus}: $\Lambda_\Omega(R):=\sup\big\{\|g_Q\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}:\ \|Q\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq R\big\}$ is the largest variation across states of the \emph{regularization gap} $g_Q(s):=\Omega^*(Q)(s)-\max_aQ(s,a)$ between the regularized and the hard maximum. It is finite, non-decreasing in $R$ (\@gobble{lem:modulus_properties}), and governs the bias (\@gobble{prop:gap_optimal_q}).
    \end{enumerate}

title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:modulus_properties}
    Under \@gobble{assumption:convex-analytic-regularity}, the supremum defining $\Lambda_\Omega(R)$ is attained and finite for every $R\geq0$, $\Lambda_\Omega$ is non-decreasing, and $\Lambda_\Omega(0)=\tau\big(\max_s\underline{\Omega}_s-\underline{\Omega}\big)$, where $\underline{\Omega}_s:=\min_{\pi_s\in\Delta(\mathcal{A})}\Omega_s(\pi_s)$ and $\underline{\Omega}:=\min_s\underline{\Omega}_s$.

name: Properties of $\Lambda_\Omega$

title: Proof
body_md: Since $\Omega^*(Q)(s)$ depends on $Q$ only through $Q_s$, \@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(iii) applied state by state shows that $\Omega^*(Q)(s)$ and $\max_aQ_s(a)$ both increase by $c$ when $Q_s$ is replaced by $Q_s+c\mathbf{1}$: $g_Q$ is invariant under the addition of a constant to each $Q_s$ separately. We may therefore restrict the supremum to the $Q$ with $\max_aQ_s(a)=0$ for every $s$, for which $\|Q\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq R$ reads $Q_s\in[-R,0]^\mathcal{A}$: a compact set. On it, $Q\mapsto\|g_Q\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}$ is continuous, since $\Omega^*$ is non-expansive in $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ (\@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(v)) and $Q\mapsto\max_aQ(\cdot,a)$ is $1$-Lipschitz; hence the supremum is attained and finite. It is non-decreasing in $R$ because the feasible set grows with $R$. Finally, for $R=0$ each $Q_s$ is a constant $c_s\mathbf{1}$, so $\Omega^*(Q)(s)=c_s+\Omega^*(0)(s)=c_s-\tau\underline{\Omega}_s$, the minimum defining $\underline{\Omega}_s$ being attained since $\Omega_s$ is closed on the compact simplex. Thus $g_Q=-\tau(\underline{\Omega}_s)_{s\in\mathcal{S}}$, whose span is $\tau(\max_s\underline{\Omega}_s-\underline{\Omega})$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $\pi$ be an admissible stationary policy.
    Iterating $V^\lambda\geq\mathcal{E}^\lambda_\pi V^\lambda$ (\@gobble{lem:discounted_fixed_point}) $K$ times, the operator $\mathcal{E}^\lambda_\pi$ being monotone, and using the Markov property we obtain $V^\lambda(s)\geq\left(\mathcal{E}^\lambda_\pi\right)^K V^\lambda(s)=\mathbb{E}_\pi\left[\sum_{t<K}\lambda^t\tilde{r}_\pi(s_t)|s_0=s\right]+\lambda^K P^K_\pi V^\lambda(s)$.
    Since $V^\lambda$ is a finite vector and $P^K_\pi$ is row-stochastic, $\left\|\lambda^K P^K_\pi V^\lambda\right\|_{\mathcal{S},\infty}\leq\lambda^K\|V^\lambda\|_{\mathcal{S},\infty}\to0$ as $K\to+\infty$ at fixed $\lambda$, so $V^\lambda\geq J^\lambda_\pi$.
    The same computation with $\pi=\pi^\lambda$, for which $V^\lambda=\mathcal{E}^\lambda_{\pi^\lambda}V^\lambda$ holds with equality, gives $V^\lambda=J^\lambda_{\pi^\lambda}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
By~\eqref{eq:existence_constants}, every admissible $\pi$ satisfies the one-sided bound $\tilde{r}_\pi\leq\|r\|_\infty-\tau\underline{\Omega}_s\leq R_{\max}$, while the policy $\tilde{\pi}$ of \@gobble{assumption:reference_policy_general} satisfies the two-sided bound $\lvert\tilde{r}_{\tilde{\pi}}(s)\rvert\leq\|r\|_\infty+\tau\lvert\Omega_s(\tilde{\pi}_s)\rvert\leq R_{\max}$.
    Bounding the summand of $J^\lambda_\pi$ termwise and summing the geometric series therefore gives $J^\lambda_\pi\leq\frac{R_{\max}}{1-\lambda}$ for every admissible $\pi$, and $J^\lambda_{\tilde{\pi}}\geq-\frac{R_{\max}}{1-\lambda}$.
    Since $V^\lambda$ is the maximum of $J^\lambda_\pi$ over admissible $\pi$ (\@gobble{lem:variational_representation}), the upper bound propagates to $V^\lambda$ and the lower bound is inherited from the single policy $\tilde{\pi}$, whence $\|V^\lambda\|_{\mathcal{S},\infty}\leq\frac{R_{\max}}{1-\lambda}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $(s_0,a_0)\in\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}$ and set, for $\lambda\in[\lambda_0,1)$, $\bar{Q}^\lambda:=Q^\lambda-Q^\lambda(s_0,a_0)\mathbf{1}$ and $\rho^\lambda:=(1-\lambda)Q^\lambda(s_0,a_0)$.

    By translation equivariance of $\Omega^*$ (\@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(iii)) and $P\mathbf{1}=\mathbf{1}$, substituting $Q^\lambda=\bar{Q}^\lambda+Q^\lambda(s_0,a_0)\mathbf{1}$ into~\eqref{eq:discounted_Q} and subtracting $\lambda Q^\lambda(s_0,a_0)$ gives
    \begin{equation}
        \label{eq:normalized_discounted}
        \bar{Q}^\lambda(s,a)+\rho^\lambda=r(s,a)+\lambda\sum_{s'}p(s'|s,a)\,\Omega^*\!\left(\bar{Q}^\lambda\right)(s').
    \end{equation}

    By \@gobble{lem:uniform_sup_bound}, $\lvert\rho^\lambda\rvert\leq(1-\lambda)\|Q^\lambda\|_\infty\leq2R_{\max}$.
    By~\eqref{eq:discounted_Q} and \@gobble{lem:row-stochastic-span}, $\|Q^\lambda\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq\|r\|_\mathrm{sp}+\lambda\|V^\lambda\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}\leq\|r\|_\mathrm{sp}+C_V$ under \@gobble{assumption:span_bounded}, hence $\|\bar{Q}^\lambda\|_\infty=\max_{s,a}\lvert Q^\lambda(s,a)-Q^\lambda(s_0,a_0)\rvert\leq\|Q^\lambda\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq\|r\|_\mathrm{sp}+C_V$.
    Both bounds are uniform in $\lambda\in[\lambda_0,1)$.

    Let $\lambda_n\uparrow1$ with $\lambda_n\geq\lambda_0$.
    The pairs $(\bar{Q}^{\lambda_n},\rho^{\lambda_n})$ lie in a compact subset of $\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}}\times\mathbb{R}$, so by Bolzano--Weierstrass some subsequence $\lambda_{\varphi(n)}\uparrow1$ satisfies $\bar{Q}^{\lambda_{\varphi(n)}}\to Q^*_\Omega$ and $\rho^{\lambda_{\varphi(n)}}\to\rho^*_\Omega$.
    Since $\Omega^*$ is non-expansive hence continuous, letting $n\to+\infty$ in~\eqref{eq:normalized_discounted} gives $Q^*_\Omega+\rho^*_\Omega\mathbf{1}=r+P\,\Omega^*(Q^*_\Omega)=\mathcal{T}_\Omega(Q^*_\Omega)$.
    The bounds are preserved in the limit.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $G_K(s)$ denote the right-hand side of~\eqref{eq:stopped_comparison}, empty sums being $0$.
    We show $V^\lambda\geq G_K$ pointwise by induction on $K$, simultaneously over all states.

    For $K=0$ we have $\sigma\wedge0=0$, so $G_0=V^\lambda$ for every $\pi$.
    Assume $V^\lambda\geq G_K$.
    If $s\in\mathcal{B}$ then $\sigma=0$ and $G_{K+1}(s)=V^\lambda(s)$.
    If $s\notin\mathcal{B}$ then $\sigma\geq1$, so splitting off the first step and applying the Markov property at $s_1$ gives $G_{K+1}(s)=\tilde{r}_\pi(s)+\lambda\left(P_\pi G_K\right)(s)$; the induction hypothesis, $P_\pi$ being non-negative, and \@gobble{lem:discounted_fixed_point} then give
    \begin{equation*}
        G_{K+1}(s)\ \leq\ \tilde{r}_\pi(s)+\lambda\left(P_\pi V^\lambda\right)(s)\ =\ \left(\mathcal{E}^\lambda_\pi V^\lambda\right)(s)\ \leq\ V^\lambda(s).
    \end{equation*}
    Both inequalities are equalities at $\pi^\lambda$, which attains the state-wise maximum of \@gobble{lem:discounted_fixed_point}, whence the equality case.

    For the last claim, $\mathcal{S}$ is finite and $\pi$ is admissible, so $\max_s\lvert\tilde{r}_\pi(s)\rvert$ and $\|V^\lambda\|_{\mathcal{S},\infty}$ are finite and the integrand of~\eqref{eq:stopped_comparison} is bounded, uniformly in $K$, by $\frac{\max_s\lvert\tilde{r}_\pi(s)\rvert}{1-\lambda}+\|V^\lambda\|_{\mathcal{S},\infty}$.
    On $\{\sigma<+\infty\}$ we have $\sigma\wedge K=\sigma$ for $K$ large enough, so the integrand converges almost surely to its value at $\sigma$; conclude by dominated convergence.

    Under \@gobble{assumption:weakly_communicating} there is $L<+\infty$ with $\mathbb{E}_\pi[\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}|s_0 = s]\leq L$ for every stationary policy $\pi$ and every $s\in\mathcal{S}$, where $\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}:=\inf\{t\geq0 | s_t\in\mathcal{C}\}$.

name: Uniformly bounded absorption time

title: Proof
body_md:
This is the uniform-transience estimate underlying stochastic shortest path problems \citep[\S3.1]{bertsekas2012dynamic}; we give the short argument.
    Let $n:=\lvert\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{tr}}\rvert$, and fix a stationary $\pi$ and $s\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{tr}}$.
    If $\mathbb{P}_\pi(\forall t, s_t\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{tr}} | s_0 = s)>0$, then with positive probability some state of the finite set $\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{tr}}$ is visited infinitely often, hence is recurrent for $P_\pi$, contradicting \@gobble{assumption:weakly_communicating}.(iii).
    So $\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}<+\infty$ a.s., and deleting cycles from a path reaching $\mathcal{C}$ gives $\mathbb{P}_\pi(\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}>n | s_0 = s)<1$.
    The map $\pi\mapsto\mathbb{P}_\pi(\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}>n | s_0 = s)$ is polynomial, hence continuous on the compact $\prod_s\Delta(\mathcal{A})$, so $\theta:=\max_{s\in\mathcal{S}_{\mathrm{tr}}}\max_\pi\mathbb{P}_\pi(\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}>n | s_0 = s)<1$; the Markov property gives $\mathbb{P}_\pi(\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}>kn | s_0 = s)\leq\theta^k$ and $\mathbb{E}_\pi[\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}|s_0 = s] = \sum_{j\geq0}\mathbb{P}_\pi(\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}>j | s_0 = s)\leq n\sum_{k\geq 0}\mathbb{P}_\pi(\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}>kn | s_0 = s)\leq\frac{n}{1-\theta}=:L$.
    If $s\in\mathcal{C}$ then $\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}=0$, so the bound holds for every $s\in\mathcal{S}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $s,s'\in\mathcal{C}$. By \@gobble{assumption:weakly_communicating}.(ii) there are $\pi$ and $k$ with $P^k_\pi(s'|s)>0$, hence a path $s=s_0,\dots,s_k=s'$ with $p(s_{i+1}|s_i,a_i)>0$ for some actions $a_i$; it stays in $\mathcal{C}$, which is closed, and deleting its cycles leaves a simple path, so $k(s,s')\leq\max\{1,\lvert\mathcal{C}\rvert-1\}$.     Since $\tilde\pi$ has full support, $P_{\tilde{\pi}}(s_{i+1}|s_i)\geq\tilde{\pi}(a_i|s_i)p(s_{i+1}|s_i,a_i)>0$ along that path, so $P^{k(s,s')}_{\tilde{\pi}}(s'|s)>0$; taking for $K^\star$ the largest of these lengths and for $p^\star$ the smallest of these finitely many positive numbers proves that admissible constants exist, and they involve only $p$ and $\tilde{\pi}$. Note also that $\tilde{\pi}$ is admissible by \@gobble{assumption:reference_policy_general} and $\pi^\lambda=\nabla\Omega^*(Q^\lambda)$ is admissible as a maximizer, so \@gobble{lem:stopped_comparison} applies to both, with $\lvert\tilde{r}_{\tilde{\pi}}\rvert\leq R_{\max}$ and $\tilde{r}_\pi\leq R_{\max}$ for every admissible $\pi$ by~\eqref{eq:existence_constants}.

    We first bound the span on $\mathcal{C}$. Fix $\lambda\in[\lambda_0,1)$ and let $s_{\max}$ and $s_{\min}$ maximize and minimize $V^\lambda$ over $\mathcal{C}$; if $s_{\max}=s_{\min}$ that span vanishes and there is nothing to prove, so assume $s_{\max}\neq s_{\min}$ and set $K:=k(s_{\min},s_{\max})\geq1$ and $p:=P^K_{\tilde{\pi}}(s_{\max}|s_{\min})\geq p^\star$. Applying \@gobble{lem:stopped_comparison} at $s_{\min}$ with $\mathcal{B}=\emptyset$, so that $\sigma\wedge K=K$, with $\pi=\tilde{\pi}$ and $\sum_{t<K}\lambda^t\leq K$, gives $V^\lambda(s_{\min})\geq -KR_{\max}+\lambda^K\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\pi}}[V^\lambda(s_K)\mid s_0=s_{\min}]$. As $\mathcal{C}$ is closed, $s_K\in\mathcal{C}$ almost surely, so $V^\lambda(s_K)\geq V^\lambda(s_{\min})$ pointwise and, isolating the event $\{s_K=s_{\max}\}$ of probability $p$, $\mathbb{E}_{\tilde{\pi}}[V^\lambda(s_K)\mid s_0=s_{\min}]\geq pV^\lambda(s_{\max})+(1-p)V^\lambda(s_{\min})$. Rearranging, the coefficient of $V^\lambda(s_{\min})$ being $1-\lambda^K$, and using $1-\lambda^K\leq K(1-\lambda)$ with \@gobble{lem:uniform_sup_bound},
    \begin{equation*}
        p\,\lambda^K\left(V^\lambda(s_{\max})-V^\lambda(s_{\min})\right)\ \leq\ KR_{\max}+\left(1-\lambda^K\right)V^\lambda(s_{\min})\ \leq\ 2KR_{\max}.
    \end{equation*}
    Since $K\leq K^\star$ and $\lambda^K\geq\lambda_0^{K^\star}=\left(1-\frac{1}{2K^\star}\right)^{K^\star}\geq\frac12$, we get $\left\|V^\lambda|_{\mathcal{C}}\right\|_{\mathcal{C},\mathrm{sp}}\leq 4K^\star R_{\max}/p^\star=:C_{\mathcal{C}}$.

    It remains to pass from $\mathcal{C}$ to $\mathcal{S}$. Write $\sigma:=\sigma_{\mathcal{C}}$ and fix $s\in\mathcal{S}$. By \@gobble{lem:uniform_absorption}, $\mathbb{E}_\pi[\sigma\mid s_0=s]\leq L$ for every stationary $\pi$, so $\sigma<+\infty$ almost surely and \@gobble{lem:stopped_comparison} applies with $\mathcal{B}=\mathcal{C}$ and the stopping time $\sigma$ itself. Its two terms are each bounded by $LR_{\max}$: the reward term because $\sum_{t<\sigma}\lambda^t\leq\sigma$, and the boundary term, once written as $\mathbb{E}_\pi[V^\lambda(s_\sigma)\mid s_0=s]+\mathbb{E}_\pi[(\lambda^\sigma-1)V^\lambda(s_\sigma)\mid s_0=s]$, because $0\leq 1-\lambda^\sigma\leq\sigma(1-\lambda)$ and $(1-\lambda)\|V^\lambda\|_{\mathcal{S},\infty}\leq R_{\max}$ by \@gobble{lem:uniform_sup_bound}. Since $s_\sigma\in\mathcal{C}$, the previous paragraph gives $0\leq V^\lambda(s_\sigma)-V^\lambda(s_{\min})\leq C_{\mathcal{C}}$. Taking $\pi=\pi^\lambda$, for which \@gobble{lem:stopped_comparison} holds with equality, and $\tilde{r}_{\pi^\lambda}\leq R_{\max}$, yields $V^\lambda(s)\leq V^\lambda(s_{\min})+C_{\mathcal{C}}+2LR_{\max}$; taking $\pi=\tilde{\pi}$ and $\tilde{r}_{\tilde{\pi}}\geq-R_{\max}$ yields $V^\lambda(s)\geq V^\lambda(s_{\min})-2LR_{\max}$. Both hold for every $s$, so $\left\|V^\lambda\right\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}\leq C_{\mathcal{C}}+4LR_{\max}=C_V$.

title: Proof
body_md:
The converse is translation equivariance (\@gobble{cor:T_omega_props}).
    Directly, $\rho_1=\rho_2$ by \@gobble{prop:uniqueness_gain}, so $h:=Q_1-Q_2$ satisfies $h=\mathcal{T}_\Omega(Q_1)-\mathcal{T}_\Omega(Q_2)=K_{\bar{\pi}}h$ by \@gobble{lem:mixing-properties-of-regularization}.(i), where $\bar{\pi}:=\bar{\pi}_{\Omega,[Q_1,Q_2]}$: the function $h$ is harmonic for the state-action kernel $K_{\bar{\pi}}$.

    By \@gobble{def:mixing_objects}.(i), $\bar{\pi}$ is a mixture of greedy policies, hence has full support, so $P_{\bar{\pi}}(s'|s)>0$ exactly when $s\to s'$ in $G$.
    The recurrent classes of the state chain are therefore the terminal strongly connected components of $G$, and there is only one, $\mathcal{C}$, by \@gobble{assumption:unique_terminal_class}; since $\bar{\pi}(a|s)>0$ for every $a$, the state-action chain has $\mathcal{C}\times\mathcal{A}$ as its unique recurrent class.
    A bounded harmonic function of a finite Markov chain is constant on each recurrent class \citep[App.~A.4]{puterman1994markov}, and on a transient $s$ we have $h(s,a)=\mathbb{E}[h(s_n,a_n)|s_0 = s, a_0 = a]$ for every $n$, which converges by absorption to the value of $h$ on that unique class.
    Hence $h$ is constant.

\label{prop:gain_interpretation}
    Let $(Q^*_\Omega,\rho^*_\Omega)$ solve~\eqref{eq:fixed_point_equation} and set $\pi^*:=\pi_{\Omega,Q^*_\Omega}$.
    For an admissible stationary policy $\pi$ define the regularized gain $\tilde{\rho}_\pi(s):=\liminf_{n\to+\infty}\frac{1}{n}\mathbb{E}_\pi\left[\sum_{t=0}^{n-1}\tilde{r}_\pi(s_t) | s_0 = s\right]$.

title: Proof
body_md:

    Equality holds throughout for $\pi=\pi^*$.

title: Proof
body_md:
This is the regularized form of the classical value-iteration bounds on the gain \citep[\S8.5.5]{puterman1994markov}, \citep[\S4.3]{bertsekas2012dynamic}.
    By monotonicity and translation equivariance of $\mathcal{T}_\Omega$ (\@gobble{cor:T_omega_props}), $\mathcal{T}^{n+1}_\Omega(Q)\leq \mathcal{T}^n_\Omega(Q+c_+\mathbf{1})=\mathcal{T}^n_\Omega(Q)+c_+\mathbf{1}$, so $\mathcal{T}^n_\Omega(Q)\leq Q+nc_+\mathbf{1}$ by induction.
    Since $\mathcal{T}_\Omega$ is non-expansive for $\|\cdot\|_\infty$ (\@gobble{cor:T_omega_props}), with $d:=\|Q-Q^*_\Omega\|_\infty$ we get $Q^*_\Omega+n\rho^*_\Omega\mathbf{1}=\mathcal{T}^n_\Omega(Q^*_\Omega)\leq \mathcal{T}^n_\Omega(Q)+d\mathbf{1}\leq Q+nc_+\mathbf{1}+d\mathbf{1}$.

title: Proof
body_md: The upper bound is \@gobble{prop:gain_interpretation}. For the lower bound, let $\mathcal{T}^\pi(U)(s,a):=r(s,a)+\sum_{s'}p(s'|s,a)\big(\langle\pi_{s'},U_{s'}\rangle-\tau\Omega_{s'}(\pi_{s'})\big)$ be the regularized evaluation operator of $\pi$; it is monotone and translation equivariant, and $\mathcal{T}^\pi(Q)=\mathcal{T}_\Omega(Q)$ since $\pi$ is greedy for $Q$. With $u:=Q-Q^*_\Omega$, \@gobble{lem:mixing-properties-of-regularization}.(i) gives $\mathcal{T}_\Omega(Q)-Q-\rho^*_\Omega\mathbf{1}=K_{\bar\pi}u-u\geq-\|u\|_\mathrm{sp}\mathbf{1}$, the entries of $K_{\bar\pi}u$ lying in $[\min u,\max u]$. Hence $\mathcal{T}^\pi(Q)\geq Q+(\rho^*_\Omega-\|u\|_\mathrm{sp})\mathbf{1}$ and, as in the proof of \@gobble{lem:gain_sandwich}, $(\mathcal{T}^\pi)^n(Q)\geq Q+n(\rho^*_\Omega-\|u\|_\mathrm{sp})\mathbf{1}$. Since $(\mathcal{T}^\pi)^n(Q)(s,a)$ is $r(s,a)$ plus the expected sum of $\tilde{r}_\pi(s_t)$, $1\leq t<n$, along $\pi$ from $(s,a)$, up to a bounded term, dividing by $n$ gives $\tilde{\rho}_\pi(s)\geq\rho^*_\Omega-\|u\|_\mathrm{sp}$. Next, $\langle\pi_s,r_s\rangle=\tilde{r}_\pi(s)+\tau\Omega_s(\pi_s)\geq\tilde{r}_\pi(s)+\tau\underline{\Omega}$, whence $\rho^\pi\geq\tilde{\rho}_\pi+\tau\underline{\Omega}$. Finally, \@gobble{cor:gain_gap_vanishes} gives $\rho^*-\rho^*_\Omega\leq\tau\overline{\Omega}$, and $\rho^*-\rho^\pi\leq(\rho^*-\rho^*_\Omega)+\|u\|_\mathrm{sp}-\tau\underline{\Omega}\leq\|u\|_\mathrm{sp}+\tau\Delta_\Omega$.

Then $\Omega_{\epsilon,s}$ is proper, closed, and $\frac{\sigma}{1-\epsilon}$-strongly convex, with effective domain $\Phi_{\epsilon,s}(\mathrm{dom}(\Omega_{0,s}))$; in particular $\Omega_\epsilon$ satisfies \@gobble{assumption:convex-analytic-regularity}, and it satisfies \@gobble{assumption:reference_policy} whenever $\Omega_0$ does.         \item \emph{Conjugate}: $\Omega^*_\epsilon(Q)(s) = \epsilon\langle\mu_s,Q_s\rangle + (1-\epsilon)\Omega^*_0(Q)(s)$; in particular $\Omega^*_\epsilon$ is differentiable with Lipschitz gradient.

In particular, if $\Omega_0$ satisfies the assumptions of \@gobble{rem:bounded_modulus}, then $\Lambda_{\Omega_\epsilon}(R)\leq\epsilon R+(1-\epsilon)\tau\Delta_{\Omega_0}$.

title: Proof
body_md:
Three ingredients drive the analysis. First, since $\nabla\Omega^*$ is the greedy policy, differences of regularized Bellman operators are kernels of average-path policies (\@gobble{lem:mixing-properties-of-regularization}); unlike the single randomized policy that represents differences of hard maxima \citep[Lemma~B.6]{chen2026contraction}, this policy inherits the domination of the greedy policies, which turns the Doeblin condition on $\mu$ into a Doeblin condition on every product of $m$ such kernels, much as lower bounds on learning policies transfer irreducibility in discounted on-policy $Q$-learning \citep{nanda2026minimal}. Second, we analyze the unmodified one-step update although $\mathcal{T}_\Omega$ only contracts over $m$ steps: expanding the Jacobian of a block of relaxed updates as an expectation over Bernoulli selections shows that the step size acts as a lazy transformation of the state-action kernels, the counterpart of the aperiodicity transformation of \citet[\S8.5.4]{puterman1994markov}, so that blocks with at least $m$ selected updates inherit the $m$-step contraction. This avoids both the multi-step estimators of \citet{zhang2021finite} and the lazy transformation of the dynamics of \citet{chen2026contraction}. Third, since the contraction rate degrades with the radius, a stopping-time argument keeps the iterates, with high probability, in a ball on which the rate holds, with a self-consistent choice of the radius.

Throughout this section, \@gobble{assumption:m-step-mixing,assumption:convex-analytic-regularity,assumption:reference_policy} and~\eqref{eq:P1} hold, and $Q^*_\Omega$ denotes a solution of~\eqref{eq:fixed_point_equation}, unique up to an additive constant (\@gobble{thm:regularized_fixed_point}); every quantity below is invariant under the choice of that constant. The $Q$-iteration bound is the regularized counterpart of the span-contraction analysis of relative value iteration \citep[\S8.5]{puterman1994markov}. For $Q$-learning, we first analyze the noiseless relaxed flow, which contracts over blocks of updates (\@gobble{subsubsec:synchronous_full_knowledge_updates}), then track the stochastic iterates along this flow up to their exit time from a span ball (\@gobble{subsubsec:sync_stochastic}); the epoch algorithm follows the same scheme, with batch averaging and a cover-time bound (\@gobble{subsec:proofs_epoch_q_learning}).

The results for general step-size schedules use the following assumption.

\begin{assumption}[Step sizes]
    \label{assumption:lr}
    The sequence of step sizes $(\alpha_t)_{t\geq 0}$ is non-increasing, satisfies $0<\alpha_t\leq1$ for all $t\geq 0$, and $\sum_{t\geq 0} \alpha_t=+\infty$.
\end{assumption}

title: Proof
body_md:
Let $Q^*_\Omega$ be given by \@gobble{thm:regularized_fixed_point}. By translation equivariance (\@gobble{cor:T_omega_props}), $\mathcal{T}^k_\Omega(Q^*_\Omega)=Q^*_\Omega+k\rho^*_\Omega\mathbf{1}$ for every $k\geq0$ and, since the projection $\Pi$ subtracts a constant, $Q_{j+k}=\mathcal{T}^k_\Omega(Q_j)-c\mathbf{1}$ for some $c\in\mathbb{R}$. Since $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$ annihilates constants, $e_{j+k}=\|\mathcal{T}^k_\Omega(Q_j)-\mathcal{T}^k_\Omega(Q^*_\Omega)\|_\mathrm{sp}$ for every $j,k\geq0$. With $k=1$, the non-expansiveness of $\mathcal{T}_\Omega$ in $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$ (\@gobble{cor:T_omega_props}) shows that $(e_j)_j$ is non-increasing.

    With $k=m$, \@gobble{lem:mixing-properties-of-regularization}.(iv) applied to $(Q_j,Q^*_\Omega)$ gives~\eqref{eq:q-iteration-rate}, since $\gamma_\Omega$ is non-increasing and $R[\mathcal{T}_\Omega^k(Q_j),\mathcal{T}_\Omega^k(Q_\Omega^*)]\leq\|Q^*_\Omega\|_\mathrm{asp}+e_j$ for $k\in\llbracket0,m-1\rrbracket$. Indeed, $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{asp}$ is invariant under constants, so $\|\mathcal{T}^k_\Omega(Q^*_\Omega)\|_\mathrm{asp}=\|Q^*_\Omega\|_\mathrm{asp}$, and the triangle inequality together with $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}$ gives $\|\mathcal{T}^k_\Omega(Q_j)\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq\|Q^*_\Omega\|_\mathrm{asp}+e_{j+k}\leq\|Q^*_\Omega\|_\mathrm{asp}+e_j$.

    Finally, $e_j\leq e_0$ for every $j$ and $\gamma_\Omega$ is non-increasing, so each factor in~\eqref{eq:q-iteration-rate} is at most $1-\beta_m\gamma_\Omega(\|Q^*_\Omega\|_\mathrm{asp}+e_0)^{m-1}\leq1-\tilde\beta$. Hence $e_{km}\leq(1-\tilde\beta)^ke_0\leq e^{-\tilde\beta k}e_0$, which is at most $\varepsilon$ for $k\geq\tilde\beta^{-1}\log(e_0/\varepsilon)$, and monotonicity extends the bound to every $j\geq km$. title: Proof

Each $K_k$ is row-stochastic, hence so is $K_{\mathcal{C}}$, and (ii) follows from \@gobble{lem:row-stochastic-span}.

With \@gobble{convention:product_order}, the Markov chain associated with $K_{\mathcal{C}}=K_{k_n}\cdots K_{k_1}$ applies the factors in the order $K_{k_n},K_{k_{n-1}},\dots,K_{k_1}$. body_md:
\label{lem:stopped-noise}

Then $\widehat{W}_{t+1}$ is $\mathcal{F}_{t+1}$-measurable, $\mathbb{E}\left[\widehat{W}_{t+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_t\right]=0$, and each entry $\widehat{W}_{t+1}(s,a)$ lies in an $\mathcal{F}_t$-measurable interval containing $0$ and of length at most $\bar{w}(R)$; in particular $\left\|\widehat{W}_{t+1}\right\|_\infty\leq\bar{w}(R)$. name: Stopped noise

title: Proof
body_md: Since $\sigma_R$ is a stopping time, $\{t<\sigma_R\}=\{\sigma_R\leq t\}^c\in\mathcal{F}_t$, so $\mathbb{E}[\widehat{W}_{t+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_t]=\mathbb{1}_{\{t<\sigma_R\}}\mathbb{E}[W_{t+1}\mid\mathcal{F}_t]=0$. Take $\kappa_0=4$ and the Chernoff bound of \@gobble{rem:chernoff_alternative}, so that $p_m\geq1-e^{-9/8}\geq\frac12$; for $\alpha\leq\frac12$, we also have $m(\kappa_0+\alpha)\leq\frac{9}{2}m$ and $C_\kappa\leq\sqrt{2}(1+9m)$, and $\alpha(e_0)\leq\frac{1}{2}$ since $\bar w\geq e_0$. We apply \@gobble{cor:sync-const-step-R} with $R=2e_0$: then $A_R=\|Q^*_\Omega\|_\mathrm{asp}+2e_0$, so that $\bar\beta(R)=p_m\tilde\beta_m(A_R)\geq\tilde\beta/2$ and $\bar w(R)=\bar w$, and the logarithm in~\eqref{eq:R-admissible-const} is at most $\iota$ since $\frac{\alpha T}{m\kappa_0}+1\leq T+1$.

    \emph{Admissibility.} The left-hand side of~\eqref{eq:R-admissible-const} is at most $\sqrt2(1+9m)\bar w\sqrt{\frac92m\alpha\iota}=3(1+9m)\bar w\sqrt{m\alpha\iota}$, which is at most $\frac{\tilde\beta}{2+\tilde\beta}e_0$ when $\alpha\leq\alpha(e_0)$. Since $x\mapsto\frac{x}{1+x}$ is increasing and $\bar\beta(R)\geq\tilde\beta/2$, this is at most $\frac{\bar\beta(R)}{1+\bar\beta(R)}(R-e_0)$, which is~\eqref{eq:R-admissible-const}.

    \emph{Bound.} With probability at least $1-\delta$, \@gobble{thm:sync-stoch-R-app} thus gives $\sup_{t\leq T}e_t\leq2e_0$. Since $\bar\beta(R)\geq\tilde\beta/2$, $I(T)\geq0$, and $I(T)>\frac{\alpha T}{m(\kappa_0+\alpha)}-1\geq\frac{2\alpha T}{9m}-1$, its contraction term satisfies $(1-\bar\beta(R))^{I(T)}e_0\leq(1-\tilde\beta/2)^{I(T)}e_0\leq(1-\tilde\beta/2)^{\frac{2\alpha T}{9m}-1}e_0$. Since $x\mapsto(1+x)/x$ is non-increasing, the noise term of \@gobble{cor:sync-const-step-R} is at most $\frac{2+\tilde\beta}{\tilde\beta}\,3(1+9m)\bar w\sqrt{m\alpha\iota}$. This is~\eqref{eq:sync-stoch-main}.

    \emph{Sample complexity.} For $\varepsilon\in(0,e_0)$, the choice $\alpha=\alpha(\varepsilon/2)\leq\alpha(e_0)$ makes the noise term equal to $\varepsilon/2$, and $(1-\tilde\beta/2)^x\leq e^{-\tilde\beta x/2}$ makes the contraction term at most $\varepsilon/2$ as soon as $T\geq\frac{9m}{\alpha\tilde\beta}\log\left(\frac{2e_0}{(1-\tilde\beta/2)\varepsilon}\right)$, which is possible since $\iota$ depends on $T$ only logarithmically. With $\alpha(\varepsilon/2)=\tilde\Theta\big(\tilde\beta^2\varepsilon^2/(m^3\bar w^2)\big)$, this gives $\tilde O\big(m^4\bar w^2/(\tilde\beta^3\varepsilon^2)\big)$ iterations, each drawing $|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|$ transitions. Since the radius is $2e_0$, the constants $\tilde\beta$ and $\bar w$ do not depend on $\varepsilon$.

\label{prop:ep_wellposed}
    For every $j\geq0$, $\ell_j<+\infty$ almost surely. Consequently convention~\eqref{eq:ep_convention_infinite} is vacuous, the extension of \@gobble{conv:ep_extended} is almost surely never used, and \@gobble{alg:epoch_regularized_q_learning} produces the update~\eqref{eq:ep_update} at every epoch almost surely.

name: Well-posedness

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $j$. For every deterministic $u\geq0$ and every $\delta'\in(0,1)$, integrating~\eqref{eq:ep_conditional_length} gives
    \begin{equation*}
        \mathbb{P}\left(\ell_j=+\infty\right)
        \ \leq\ \mathbb{P}\left(\left\{\ell_j>L(u,\delta')\right\}\cap\mathcal{D}_j(u)\right)+\mathbb{P}\left(\mathcal{D}_j(u)^c\right)
        \ \leq\ \delta'+\mathbb{P}\left(\|Q_j\|_\mathrm{asp}>u\right).
    \end{equation*}
    Letting $\delta'\downarrow0$ at fixed $u$ gives $\mathbb{P}(\ell_j=+\infty)\leq\mathbb{P}(\|Q_j\|_\mathrm{asp}>u)$ for every $u$, and letting $u\uparrow+\infty$ gives $\mathbb{P}(\ell_j=+\infty)=0$, since $\|Q_j\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq2\|Q_j\|_\infty<+\infty$ everywhere by \@gobble{lem:ep_update}.(ii).

label: lem:ep_counts
title: Lemma
head: environment
name: Epoch and block counts

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{(i)}. Epoch $j$ terminates only when each of the $|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|$ pairs has been visited at least $B_j$ times, and each transition visits one pair, so $\ell_j\geq|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|B_j$; summing, $J(T)|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|\underline{B}\leq n_{J(T)}\leq T$. Each sub-block is non-empty, so each block has at least $m$ epochs.

    \emph{(ii)}. By definition of $I(T)$, $b_{I(T)+1}>J(T)$, and each block consumes at most $m(\kappa_0+\alpha_0)$ (\@gobble{lem:sum_block}), so $\sum_{j<J(T)}\alpha_j\leq\sum_{j<b_{I(T)+1}}\alpha_j<(I(T)+1)m(\kappa_0+\alpha_0)$; the floor form follows since $I(T)$ is an integer. For $\alpha_j\equiv\alpha$ the stopping rule fires after exactly $\lceil\kappa_0/\alpha\rceil$ epochs.

    \emph{(iii)}. If $J(T)=J_{\max}(T)$ there is nothing to prove, since $J^-(T)\leq J_{\max}(T)$ by the bound $L_j(\delta')\geq m|\mathcal{S}||\mathcal{A}|B_j$ of \@gobble{lem:ep_cover_time}. Otherwise suppose $J(T)<J^-(T)$. Every $j\leq J(T)$ satisfies $j<\sigma_R$ and $j<J_{\max}(T)$, hence $\ell_j\leq L_j(\delta')$, so $n_{J(T)+1}=\sum_{j\leq J(T)}\ell_j\leq\sum_{j<J(T)+1}L_j(\delta')\leq T$, the last inequality because $J(T)+1\leq J^-(T)$; this contradicts the maximality of $J(T)$. The constant case follows by injecting $J(T)\geq\lfloor T/L(\delta')\rfloor$ into the exact identity of (ii) and using $\lfloor x\rfloor>x-1$ along with $\lceil\kappa_0/\alpha\rceil<(\kappa_0+\alpha)/\alpha$.

title: Proof
body_md:
\emph{(i)}. The $t_l(x)$ are stopping times for $(\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}^{(j)}_n)_n$, a.s.\ finite by \@gobble{prop:ep_wellposed}, and $t_{l-1}(x)+1\leq t_l(x)$, so $\mathcal{K}^{(j)}_{l-1}\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}^{(j)}_{t_l(x)}\subseteq\mathcal{K}^{(j)}_l$; and $t_{B_j}(x)+1\leq\ell_j$, the extended trajectory coinciding with the algorithm before $\ell_j$, gives $\mathcal{K}^{(j)}_{B_j}\subseteq\mathcal{G}_{j+1}$.

    \emph{(ii)}. On $\{t_l(x)=n\}$ we have $(\tilde{s}^{(j)}_n,\tilde{a}^{(j)}_n)=x$ and the conditional law of $\tilde{s}^{(j)}_{n+1}$ given $\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}^{(j)}_n$ is $p(\cdot\mid x)$, so $\mathbb{E}[Z^{(j)}_l(x)\mid\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}^{(j)}_{t_l(x)}]=0$. Since $\mathbb{1}_{\{j<\sigma_R\}}$ is $\mathcal{G}_j$-, hence $\mathcal{K}^{(j)}_{l-1}$-measurable and $\mathcal{K}^{(j)}_{l-1}\subseteq\widetilde{\mathcal{H}}^{(j)}_{t_l(x)}$, the tower property gives the claim.

Conditionally on $\mathcal{G}_j$, $\Omega^*(Q_j)$ is fixed, so $Z^{(j)}_l(x)$ lies in the $\mathcal{G}_j$-measurable interval of length exactly $\|\Omega^*(Q_j)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}$, translated by $-(P\Omega^*(Q_j))(x)$. title: Proof
body_md:
We apply \@gobble{cor:ep_alpha_one} with $R=2e_0$. Then $A_R=\|Q^*_\Omega\|_\mathrm{asp}+2e_0$, so that $\tilde{\beta}_m(A_R)=\tilde\beta$, $\bar{w}(R)=\bar w$ and $q_R=\bar\gamma\tilde\beta\eta_{\min}$; moreover $\iota(\delta')\leq\iota_1\leq\iota$ since $J_{\max}(T)\leq T$.

    \emph{Admissibility.} We have $2m\bar{U}\leq\sqrt2\,m\bar w\sqrt{\iota/B}$ and $1+\tilde\beta\leq2$, so~\eqref{eq:ep_admissible_alpha_one} holds as soon as $\sqrt2\,m\bar w\sqrt{\iota/B}\leq\tilde\beta e_0/2$, i.e.\ $B\geq B(e_0)$.

    \emph{Bound.} With probability at least $1-\delta$, \@gobble{cor:ep_alpha_one} gives $\sup_{j\leq J(T)}e_j\leq2e_0$, and its residual term is at most $\frac{2\cdot\sqrt2\,m\bar w\sqrt{\iota/B}}{\tilde\beta}$, which gives~\eqref{eq:epoch-main-bound}. On the same event, \@gobble{prop:ep_no_escape} gives $\ell_j\leq L_j(\delta')\leq L$ for every $j<J(T)$, since $\iota(\delta')\leq\iota$, so \@gobble{lem:ep_counts}.(iii) gives $J(T)\geq\lfloor T/L\rfloor$, and $I(T)=\lfloor J(T)/m\rfloor$.

    \emph{Sample complexity.} For $\varepsilon\in(0,e_0)$, the choice $B=\lceil B(\varepsilon/2)\rceil\geq B(e_0)$ makes the residual term at most $\varepsilon/2$. For $T\geq mL\lceil\tilde\beta^{-1}\log(2e_0/\varepsilon)\rceil$, which is possible since $\iota$ depends on $T$ only logarithmically, we get $I(T)\geq\tilde\beta^{-1}\log(2e_0/\varepsilon)$, and $1-u\leq e^{-u}$ makes the contraction term at most $\varepsilon/2$. Since $L=\tilde\Theta\big(mB/(\bar\gamma\tilde\beta\eta_{\min})\big)$ and $B=\tilde\Theta\big(m^2\bar w^2/(\tilde\beta\varepsilon)^2\big)$, this gives $\tilde O\big(m^4\bar w^2/(\tilde\beta^3\cdot\bar\gamma\tilde\beta\eta_{\min}\cdot\varepsilon^2)\big)$ sampled transitions.

label: rem:pl_local_mixing
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:pl_local_mixing}
    \leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item \emph{The core $\mathcal{S}_\infty$ is closed}: by (i), $\mathcal{S}_\infty=\mathcal{S}_{h_1+1}=F(\mathcal{S}_{h_1})=F(\mathcal{S}_\infty)$. On the MDP restricted to $\mathcal{S}_\infty$, (ii) is \@gobble{assumption:m-step-mixing} with a full-support $\nu$, so \@gobble{thm:regularized_fixed_point} gives $(Q^*_\Omega,\rho^*_\Omega)$ on $\mathcal{S}_\infty\times\mathcal{A}$, with $Q^*_\Omega$ unique up to an additive constant under~\eqref{eq:P1}.
        \item \emph{Global case}: if \@gobble{assumption:m-step-mixing} holds, then $K^m_\mu(s'|s,a)>0$ for all $(s,a,s')$, so $\mathcal{S}_h=\mathcal{S}$ for $h\geq m$ and \@gobble{assumption:pl_local_mixing} holds with $\mathcal{S}_\infty=\mathcal{S}$ and $h_1=m$. The spatial localization is then vacuous, and only the temporal one remains.
        \item \emph{Transient layers}: nothing is assumed on $\mathcal{S}_0,\dots,\mathcal{S}_{h_1-1}$, which enter the analysis only through $\bar S_H$ and the coverage of the shallow levels (\@gobble{lem:pl_coverage}).
        \item \emph{When (i) holds}: $\mathcal{S}_h$ is the set of states reachable in exactly $h$ steps from $\mathrm{supp}(\xi)$ in the union graph $G$ (\@gobble{def:union_graph}), so $(\mathcal{S}_h)_h$ is eventually periodic, and (i) holds for some finite $h_1$ as soon as every strongly connected component of $G$ that contains a cycle and is reachable from $\mathrm{supp}(\xi)$ is aperiodic, e.g.\ contains a state $s$ with $p(s|s,a)>0$ for some $a$: closed walks in such a component have all large enough lengths, so a state reached at arbitrarily large depths is reached at every large enough depth.
    \end{enumerate}

The sweep computes $Q_h=\mathcal{T}_{\Omega,h}(Q_{h+1})$ from $Q_H=Q_B|_{\mathcal{X}_H}$, which is the definition of the planning solution, and each value $\mathcal{T}_{\Omega,h}(Q_{h+1})(s,a)$ uses the $|\mathcal{S}_{h+1}|$ probabilities $p(s'|s,a)$, $s'\in\mathcal{S}_{h+1}$, whence the count. Finally, $H_{\mathrm{eff}}\geq H_{\mathrm{eff}}(A_{\Delta_B})$, so the condition on $H$ implies~\eqref{eq:pl_depth} at $h=0$.

label: lem:pl_sync_nilpotent
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pl_sync_nilpotent}
    Let $(Q_{j,h})_{j\geq0,\,h\leq H}$ satisfy $Q_{j+1,h}=\mathcal{T}_{\Omega,h}(Q_{j,h+1})$ for $h<H$ and $Q_{j,H}=Q_B|_{\mathcal{X}_H}$ for every $j$. Then $Q_{j,h}=Q^*_{\Omega,h}$ for every $h\leq H$ and $j\geq H-h$.
head: environment
name: Exact forgetting of the initialization

title: Proof
body_md: Backward induction on $h$. The case $h=H$ holds by assumption. If $Q_{j,h+1}=Q^*_{\Omega,h+1}$ for every $j\geq H-h-1$, then $Q_{j+1,h}=\mathcal{T}_{\Omega,h}(Q^*_{\Omega,h+1})=Q^*_{\Omega,h}$ for every such $j$, i.e.\ $Q_{j,h}=Q^*_{\Omega,h}$ for every $j\geq H-h$.

label: rem:pl_no_backward_sweep
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:pl_no_backward_sweep}
    Level $h$ at epoch $j+1$ is computed from level $h+1$ at epoch $j$, which is $\mathcal{G}_j$-measurable, hence independent of the data of epoch $j$. A single backward sweep over stored transitions would instead evaluate $\Omega^*(\widehat Q_{h+1})$ at the level-$(h+1)$ states of the very rollouts on which $\widehat Q_{h+1}$ depends, and lose the martingale structure of the noise. Restoring independence would require $H$ disjoint groups of rollouts, one per level, which costs the same factor $H$ as the $H$ epochs of \@gobble{lem:pl_sync_nilpotent}.

label: prop:pl_epoch_wellposed
title: Proposition
body_md:
\label{prop:pl_epoch_wellposed}
    Every epoch terminates almost surely, and every $Q_{j,h}$ is a finite, $\mathcal{G}_j$-measurable random vector.
head: environment
name: Well-posedness

title: Proof
body_md: Finiteness and measurability follow by induction on $j$ as in \@gobble{lem:ep_update}.(ii), each coordinate of $w_{j,h}$ being bounded by $\|Q_{j,h+1}\|_\mathrm{sp}+\|\Omega^*(0)\|_{\mathcal{S},\mathrm{sp}}$ (\@gobble{lem:omega_star_props}.(vii)). For termination, fix $j$ and a deterministic $u\geq0$. Conditionally on $\mathcal{G}_j$, the rollouts of epoch $j$ are i.i.d.\ and, on $\{\max_{h<H}\|Q_{j,h}\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq u\}\in\mathcal{G}_j$, each of them visits a given $(h,x)$, $x\in\mathcal{X}_h$, with probability at least $\min\{q_\mu,q_\pi(u)\}>0$ by \@gobble{lem:pl_coverage}. Each pair is thus visited $B$ times after finitely many rollouts, almost surely on that event, and letting $u\uparrow\infty$ concludes.

label: lem:pl_epoch_noise
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pl_epoch_noise}
    With probability at least $1-\delta/2$, $\|\widehat{w}_{j,h}\|_\infty\leq\bar{u}_j(R):=\bar{w}(R)\sqrt{\iota_H/(2B_j)}$ for all $j<J$ and $h<H$.
head: environment
name: Noise

title: Proof
body_md: Fix $(j,h,x)$ with $x\in\mathcal{X}_h$, and order the $B$ terms of $\widehat{w}_{j,h}(x)$ by the successive level-$h$ visits of $x$ during epoch $j$, the rollouts being taken in chronological order. Given $\mathcal{G}_j$ and the past of these visits, the successor of a visit is distributed as $p(\cdot|x)$, while $\Omega^*(Q_{j,h+1})$ is $\mathcal{G}_j$-measurable. The terms are therefore martingale differences, lying in $\mathcal{G}_j$-measurable intervals of length at most $\bar{w}(R)/B_j$ on $\{j<\sigma_R\}$ and vanishing off it, and their number is $B_j$ by the cap (\@gobble{lem:ep_update}). \@gobble{lem:azuma_range} with $u=\bar{u}_j(R)$ gives a failure probability $2e^{-\iota_H}$, and a union bound over the at most $JH\bar S_H|\mathcal{A}|$ triples concludes.

label: lem:pl_epoch_length
title: Lemma
body_md:
\label{lem:pl_epoch_length}
    With probability at least $1-\delta/4$, every epoch $j<J$ with $j<\sigma_R$ lasts at most $N_jH$ transitions, where $N_j:=\lceil(\sqrt{B_j}+\sqrt{\iota_H})^2/q\rceil$.

name: Epoch length

title: Proof
body_md: Conditionally on $\mathcal{G}_j$, the rollouts of epoch $j$, extended beyond its end if needed, are i.i.d., and on $\{j<\sigma_R\}\in\mathcal{G}_j$, \@gobble{lem:pl_coverage} with $\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{G}_j$ shows that each of them visits a given $(h,x)$, $x\in\mathcal{X}_h$, with probability at least $q$. As in the proof of \@gobble{lem:ep_cover_time}, the exact Chernoff bound~\eqref{eq:exact-chernoff} with $b=1$, $a=N_jq$ and $c=B_j$ bounds by $e^{-\iota_H}$ the conditional probability that fewer than $B_j$ of the first $N_j$ rollouts visit $(h,x)$, and a union bound over the at most $JH\bar S_H|\mathcal{A}|$ triples concludes. Independence across resets replaces the $m$-step sub-sampling of \@gobble{lem:ep_cover_time}.

label: thm:pl_epoch
title: Theorem

name: Finite-time bound for epoch planning

title: Proof
body_md: Work on the intersection of the events of \@gobble{lem:pl_epoch_noise,lem:pl_epoch_length}, of probability at least $1-\delta$, on which all epochs terminate (\@gobble{prop:pl_epoch_wellposed}). We prove by induction on $j\leq J$ that $\sigma_R>j$ and that~\eqref{eq:pl_epoch_bound} holds at rank $j$; the length bound then follows from \@gobble{lem:pl_epoch_length}. At $j=0$, both claims were checked above. Assume $\sigma_R>j-1$, fix $h<H$, let $\ell:=\min\{j,H-h\}$ and consider the \emph{diagonal} profile $P_l:=Q_{j-(l-h),l}$, $l\in\llbracket h,h+\ell\rrbracket$. For $l<h+\ell$, the epoch $i:=j-(l-h)-1$ satisfies $0\leq i<j\leq\sigma_R$, so~\eqref{eq:pl_epoch_update} gives $P_l=\mathcal{T}_{\Omega,l}(P_{l+1})+\widehat{w}_{i,l}$: the residuals of the diagonal are the stopped noises, and \@gobble{lem:pl_epoch_noise} and $\|\cdot\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq2\|\cdot\|_\infty$ bound their span by $2\bar{u}_i(R)$. For $l>h$, $P_l$ is either computed at epoch $j-(l-h)<j\leq\sigma_R$ or equal to $Q_B|_{\mathcal{X}_H}$, whose action span is at most $A_{\Delta_B}$ by \@gobble{lem:pl_uniform_bounds}, so $\|P_l\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq A_R$, and $A_R\geq A_{\Delta_B}$. The last element is $P_{h+\ell}=Q_B|_{\mathcal{X}_H}=Q^*_{\Omega,H}$ if $\ell=H-h$, and $P_{h+\ell}=Q_{0,h+j}$, within $D_0$ of $Q^*_{\Omega,h+j}$, if $\ell=j<H-h$. The first inequality of \@gobble{lem:pl_master} with $h_0=h$ and $h_e=h+\ell$ gives~\eqref{eq:pl_epoch_bound} at rank $j$, since $n(h,\ell)=n(h,j)$ when $\ell=j$. Finally, \@gobble{lem:pl_geometric_sum} and $M(h,A_R)\leq M(A_R)$ bound the sum in~\eqref{eq:pl_epoch_bound} by $2M(A_R)\max_{i<J}\bar{u}_i(R)$, so \@gobble{lem:pl_uniform_bounds} and~\eqref{eq:pl_admissible} give $\|Q_{j,h}-Q^*_\Omega\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathcal{X}_h}\leq D_0+2M(A_R)\max_{i<J}\bar{u}_i(R)+\Delta_B\leq R$ for every $h<H$, i.e.\ $\sigma_R>j$.

body_md:
We apply \@gobble{thm:pl_epoch} with $B_j\equiv B$ and $R=2e_0$, for which~\eqref{eq:pl_epoch_bound} and \@gobble{lem:pl_geometric_sum} give $2M(h,A_R)\bar u(R)$. With probability at least $1-\delta$, every epoch lasts at most $NH=H\lceil(\sqrt B+\sqrt{\iota_H})^2/q\rceil$ transitions and, since $J\geq H$, \eqref{eq:pl_epoch_bound} at $h=0$ gives $\|Q_{J,0}-Q^*_{\Omega,0}\|_\mathrm{sp}\leq2M\bar w\sqrt{\iota_H/(2B)}$. \@gobble{cor:pl_horizon_bias} at $h=0$, with $n(0,H)=\lfloor(H-h_1)/m\rfloor$ and $\tilde\beta\leq\tilde\beta_m(A_{\Delta_B})$, bounds $\|Q^*_{\Omega,0}-Q^*_\Omega\|_{\mathrm{sp},\mathcal{X}_0}$ by $(1-\tilde\beta)^{\lfloor(H-h_1)/m\rfloor}\Delta_B$, and the triangle inequality gives~\eqref{eq:pl-epoch-main}.

label: rem:pl_epoch_vs_learning
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:pl_epoch_vs_learning}
    For $h_1=0$, \@gobble{thm:pl-epoch-main} costs $\tilde O(m^4\bar w^2/(\tilde\beta^4q\varepsilon^2))$ transitions, against $\tilde O(m^4\bar w^2/(\tilde\beta^3q_R\varepsilon^2))$ for \@gobble{thm:epoch-main-body}: at equal coverage constant, epoch planning is a factor $1/\tilde\beta$ more expensive. Propagation is paid twice, once in depth, since a rollout gives one sample per level to $H$ distinct tables, and once in epochs, since $J=H$ iterations are needed to propagate the boundary to the root. Per table, planning is $m$ times more efficient, the independence across resets removing the sub-sampling of \@gobble{lem:ep_cover_time}. Merging the tables removes the extra factor (\@gobble{subsec:pl_reset_learning}).

label: lem:pl_reset_cover_time

head: environment
name: Cover time with resets

title: Proof
body_md: Conditionally on $\mathcal{G}_j$, the rollouts of epoch $j$, extended beyond its end if needed, are i.i.d. Consider the instants of depths $h_1+km$, $k\in\llbracket1,K_0\rrbracket$, of the successive rollouts, in chronological order, fix $(s,a)\in\mathcal{S}_\infty\times\mathcal{A}$, and let $Z_l$ indicate that the $l$-th instant visits $(s,a)$. On $\mathcal{D}_j(u)\in\mathcal{G}_j$, the actions at depths $h\geq h_1$ are drawn from $\mu$ or from a policy dominating $\gamma_\Omega(u)\mu$, and the $m$ steps before each instant start at a depth $h\geq h_1$, hence in $\mathcal{S}_\infty$. \@gobble{lem:pl_coverage}.(i) with $\mathcal{G}=\mathcal{G}_j$, conditional on the previous instant of the same rollout or integrated over a fresh reset, therefore gives $\mathbb{E}[Z_l\mid Z_1,\dots,Z_{l-1},\mathcal{G}_j]\geq q^{\mathrm{res}}(u)$. The rest is the proof of \@gobble{lem:ep_cover_time}: the exact Chernoff bound~\eqref{eq:exact-chernoff} with $b=1$, $a=Kq^{\mathrm{res}}(u)$ and $c=B_j$, where $K:=\lceil(\sqrt{B_j}+\sqrt{\iota(\delta')})^2/q^{\mathrm{res}}(u)\rceil$, and a union bound over $\mathcal{S}_\infty\times\mathcal{A}$ show that, with conditional probability at least $1-\delta'$, every pair is visited $B_j$ times within $K$ instants, which $\lceil K/K_0\rceil$ rollouts of $H$ transitions provide. Finally, $K_0\geq(H-1-h_1-m)/m\geq H/(2m)$ when $H\geq2(h_1+m+1)$.

title: Proof
body_md: The proofs of \@gobble{subsec:proofs_epoch_q_learning} use the trajectory through three properties only: the behavior during epoch $j$ is $\mathcal{G}_j$-measurable; given the past, the successor of a retained visit of $(s,a)$ is distributed as $p(\cdot|s,a)$ (\@gobble{lem:ep_noise}.(ii)); and the cap makes the number of retained samples deterministic (\@gobble{lem:ep_update}). title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:pl_merge}
    \leavevmode
    \begin{enumerate}[label=(\roman*)]
        \item \emph{What the resets bring.} Relative to \@gobble{thm:epoch-main-body}, \eqref{eq:pl_reset_complexity} takes $\eta_{\min}$ over $\mathcal{S}_\infty\times\mathcal{A}$, with the minorizing measure of \@gobble{assumption:pl_local_mixing}, which can be much larger when $\mathcal{S}_\infty\subsetneq\mathcal{S}$. Relative to epoch planning, merging the tables saves the factor $1/\tilde{\beta}$ of \@gobble{rem:pl_epoch_vs_learning}, and the rollout length only enters through $H\geq2(h_1+m+1)$ and the second term of~\eqref{eq:pl_reset_complexity}.
        \item \emph{The boundary becomes the initialization.} There is no horizon bias: the target is $Q^*_\Omega$ itself, and the boundary value $Q_B$ of the planners plays the role of $Q_0$. The horizon bias $(1-\tilde\beta)^{\lfloor(H-h_1)/m\rfloor}\Delta_B$ of \@gobble{thm:pl-epoch-main} and the initialization term $(1-\tilde\beta)^{\lfloor J(T)/m\rfloor}e_0$ of \@gobble{thm:epoch-main-body} are the same term under two names.

        \item \emph{A single parameterized algorithm.} Without resets, \@gobble{alg:pl_reset_learning} is \@gobble{alg:epoch_regularized_q_learning}, and \@gobble{thm:pl_reset_learning,thm:epoch-main-body} are one statement in which $(H,\xi)$ only enters through the coverage constant and the epoch length.
    \end{enumerate}

label: thm:alpha
title: Theorem
head: environment
name: The $\alpha$-divergence regularizer

title: Proof
body_md:
Fix $s$ and write $\pi_a$, $\mu_a$, $Q_a$ for $\pi_s(a)$, $\mu(a|s)$, $Q(s,a)$.

    \emph{(i)} The term $\pi_a^\alpha\mu_a^{1-\alpha}$ is finite for every $\pi_a\geq0$ when $\alpha>0$, and infinite at $\pi_a=0$ when $\alpha<0$, as is $\log(\mu_a/\pi_a)$ at $\alpha=0$. $\Omega_{\alpha,s}$ is convex and continuous on its domain and tends to $+\infty$ at the boundary when $\alpha\leq0$, hence proper and closed; $D_\alpha(\mu_s\|\mu_s)=0$ gives \@gobble{assumption:reference_policy_general} with $\tilde{\pi}=\mu$.

    \emph{(ii)} On the relative interior $\nabla^2\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\pi)=\operatorname{diag}(\pi_a^{\alpha-2}\mu_a^{1-\alpha})$, and Cauchy--Schwarz gives $\langle\nabla^2\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\pi)h,h\rangle\geq\|h\|_1^2\big/\sum_a\pi_a^{2-\alpha}\mu_a^{\alpha-1}$. For $1\leq\alpha\leq2$, H\"older bounds the sum by $(\sum_a\pi_a)^{2-\alpha}(\sum_a\mu_a)^{\alpha-1}=1$; for $\alpha<1$, $\pi_a^{2-\alpha}\leq\pi_a$ bounds it by $\mu_{\min}^{\alpha-1}$. Integrating along segments and closing by lower semicontinuity gives the modulus. For $\alpha>2$ the Hessian is positive definite on the interior but its entries vanish as $\pi_a\to0$.

    \emph{(iii)} The form~\eqref{eq:alpha_policy_1} of the maximizer, with a unique normalizer, is \citet[Proposition~1]{roulet2025loss} with reference measure $\mu_s$ and logits $Q_s/\tau$. For the bracket, $S(\zeta):=\sum_a\mu_a[1+(\alpha-1)(Q_a-\zeta)/\tau]_+^{1/(\alpha-1)}$ is continuous and non-increasing on its domain, $\mathbb{R}$ if $\alpha>1$ and $(\max_aQ_a-\tau/(1-\alpha),+\infty)$ if $\alpha<1$; $S(\max_aQ_a)\leq1$, every ratio $\pi_a/\mu_a$ being then at most $1$; and $S\geq1$ at $\zeta=\max_aQ_a-\tau(\mu_{a^*}^{1-\alpha}-1)/(\alpha-1)$, which lies in the domain and where the term of $a^*$ alone equals $1$. Finally, for $\alpha\neq0$, with $u_a:=1+(\alpha-1)(Q_a-\zeta_s)/\tau$, we have $\pi_a^\alpha\mu_a^{1-\alpha}=\pi_au_a$ and $\sum_a\pi_au_a=1+(\alpha-1)(\langle\pi,Q_s\rangle-\zeta_s)/\tau$, hence $\tau\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\pi)=(\langle\pi,Q_s\rangle-\zeta_s)/\alpha$, and $\Omega^*_\alpha(Q)(s)=\langle\pi,Q_s\rangle-\tau\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\pi)$ is~\eqref{eq:alpha_policy_2}.

    \emph{(iv)} If $\|Q\|_\mathrm{asp}\leq R$ then $Q_a-\zeta_s\geq Q_a-\max_bQ_b\geq-R$ by (iii), and $x\mapsto[1+(\alpha-1)x/\tau]_+^{1/(\alpha-1)}$ is non-decreasing for every $\alpha\neq1$, which gives the bound; $\alpha=1$ is the limit. For $\alpha>1$, take $a^*$ with $\mu_{a^*}=\mu_{\max}$, $Q_{a^*}=0$ and $Q_b=-R$ otherwise. The candidate $\pi=\delta_{a^*}$ has normalizer $\zeta=\tau(1-\mu_{\max}^{1-\alpha})/(\alpha-1)$ and $u_b=\mu_{\max}^{1-\alpha}-(\alpha-1)R/\tau\leq0$ for $b\neq a^*$ as soon as $R\geq\tau\mu_{\max}^{1-\alpha}/(\alpha-1)$; by uniqueness it is the greedy policy, so $\gamma_{\Omega_\alpha}(R)=0$. That the greedy map can be sparse for $\alpha>1$ is known \citep{peters2019sparse,roulet2025loss}; what~\eqref{eq:P1} requires, and what (iv) provides, is the uniform lower bound and the explicit threshold.

    \emph{(v)} Let $a^*\in\operatorname*{arg\,max}_aQ_a$. For $\alpha>0$, $\Omega_{\alpha,s}$ is bounded on $\Delta(\mathcal{A})$ by $0\leq\Omega_{\alpha,s}\leq\max_a\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\delta_a)=\Delta_\alpha$, the maximum of a convex function on the simplex being attained at a vertex, and the boundedness property of the conjugate \citep[Proposition~1(ii)]{geist2019theory} gives $\max_aQ_a-\tau\Delta_\alpha\leq\Omega^*_\alpha(Q)(s)\leq\max_aQ_a$; testing the maximum defining $\Omega^*_\alpha(Q)(s)$ against $\delta_{a^*}$ gives the same bound with $\mu_{a^*}$ in place of $\mu_{\min}$. For $0<\alpha<1$, $\Delta_\alpha=\frac{1-\mu_{\min}^{1-\alpha}}{\alpha(1-\alpha)}\leq\frac{1}{\alpha(1-\alpha)}$. For $\alpha\leq0$, $\Omega_{\alpha,s}$ is unbounded and we test instead $\pi^\varepsilon:=(1-\varepsilon)\delta_{a^*}+\varepsilon\mu_s$: $\langle\pi^\varepsilon,Q_s\rangle\geq\max_aQ_a-\varepsilon R$, and $\pi^\varepsilon\geq\varepsilon\mu_s$ with $x\mapsto x^\alpha$ non-increasing gives $\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\pi^\varepsilon)\leq\frac{\varepsilon^\alpha-1}{\alpha(\alpha-1)}$, with limit $\log(1/\varepsilon)$ at $\alpha=0$. Minimizing over $\varepsilon$, at $\varepsilon=\min\{1,(\tau/((1-\alpha)R))^{1/(1-\alpha)}\}$, gives~\eqref{eq:alpha_modulus}. The rates are attained with $Q_{a^*}=R$ and $Q_b=0$: writing $\pi_b=\delta$, the gap is $\min_\delta\{R\delta+\tau\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\pi)\}$ with $\Omega_{\alpha,s}(\pi)\sim\mu_b^{1-\alpha}\delta^\alpha/(\alpha(\alpha-1))$ for $\alpha<0$ and $\sim\mu_b\log(1/\delta)$ for $\alpha=0$, whose minimizer gives the same powers of $R$.

label: rem:alpha_exact
title: Remark
body_md:
\label{rem:alpha_exact}
    For a fixed $\mu$, $\zeta_s$ is non-decreasing in each $Q_a$ while $\pi_b/\mu_b$ is non-increasing in $\zeta_s-Q_b$, so the infimum defining $\gamma_\Omega(R)$ is attained with the least likely action at the bottom and every other one at $+R$; symmetrically, $\Lambda_\Omega^{\mathrm{pt}}(R)$ is attained with the least likely action alone at the top and every other one at $-R$. Both depend on $\mu$ only through $\mu_{\min}$, and the explicit normalizers give, for instance, $\gamma_\Omega(R)=\big(\mu_{\min}+(1-\mu_{\min})e^{R/\tau}\big)^{-1}$ for the reverse KL and $\gamma_\Omega(R)=[1-(1-\mu_{\min})R/\tau]_+$ for the $\chi^2$, whose limits as $\mu_{\min}\to0$ are the bounds of \@gobble{tab:alpha_family}. Inside the window $0<\alpha\leq1$ the comparison is quantitative and depends on how $\tau$ is matched across $\alpha$. At fixed $\tau$, the profile decays as $(R/\tau)^{-1/(1-\alpha)}$, more slowly for smaller $\alpha$, while the modulus constant $\Delta_\alpha=(1-\mu_{\min}^{1-\alpha})/(\alpha(1-\alpha))$ tends, as $\mu_{\min}\to0$, to $1/(\alpha(1-\alpha))$ for $\alpha<1$, minimal at the Hellinger value $4$, and to $+\infty$ at $\alpha=1$: the Hellinger regularizer is the most robust to a small $\mu_{\min}$, whereas for a balanced $\mu$ the reverse KL can have the smaller constant: for a uniform $\mu$, $\log|\mathcal{A}|<4(1-|\mathcal{A}|^{-1/2})$ as long as $|\mathcal{A}|\leq24$. The lower bound of \@gobble{thm:alpha}.(iv) equals $(f')^{-1}(-R/\tau)$ for the generator $f(u)=(u^\alpha-\alpha u+\alpha-1)/(\alpha(\alpha-1))$ of $D_\alpha$, the inverse link that also drives the policy-gradient analysis of \citet{labbi2026beyond}: their probability floor \citep[Theorem~3.5]{labbi2026beyond} is proportional to $(f')^{-1}$ evaluated at an argument of order $-1/\lambda$, where $\lambda$ is their temperature, up to factors depending on the discount and the initial distribution, and their exponential-versus-polynomial dichotomy between the KL and $\alpha<1$ is the one displayed by our profile bounds. They also find that the best $\alpha$ lies strictly inside $(0,1)$ \citep[Corollary~4.8]{labbi2026beyond}, for a different criterion.
